questions.prompt: What should this refactor include in the first implementation slice?
questions.description: The north star is broad. This chooses the smallest useful slice that makes the system model visible in code while keeping GitHub/npm and advanced policy work for later.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Refactor the current Skillpack-managed skill implementation to expose the north-star language and contracts: Skill, Skill Location, Resolved Skill, Resource Manifest, and current approved version. Keep existing CRUD and UI behavior working. Defer GitHub/npm source adapters, full trust workflow UI, policy configuration, and materialized distribution.

options.label: Rename/reshape shared API contracts around Skill and Skill Library concepts
Use skill://skillpack/{handle} as the canonical Skillpack-managed location
Make read responses represent a Resolved Skill with content and resource manifest
Introduce the current approved concept for Skillpack-managed versions with an MVP auto-approved policy
Preserve current routes and UI behavior while adding the new model internally
Also implement GitHub source indexing in this slice
Also implement configurable Delivery Policy in this slice
Also redesign the library UI around source/trust terminology

questions.prompt: How aggressively should the database schema move toward the north-star model now?
questions.description: Current tables are skills, skill_versions, and skill_resources. A deep schema rewrite could unlock source-backed entries but increases migration risk.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Use an incremental schema change: keep existing tables, add minimal fields needed for source type, handle/location, and approved version semantics. Leave full source/revision tables for the GitHub implementation ADR/goal.

options.label: Incremental: keep existing tables and add minimal north-star fields
Deep rewrite: introduce skills, skill_sources, revisions, and trust tables now
Contracts only: update API/domain naming without DB migration

questions.prompt: What should happen to existing name-based skill routes in this slice?
questions.description: Current API and SPA routes use skill name. North-star locations use skill:// locators, and future source namespaces allow duplicate names across sources.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Keep existing name-based routes for Skillpack-managed skills as compatibility routes. Add resolve-oriented API support that accepts Skill Location. Defer public URL redesign until source-backed entries exist.

options.label: Keep name routes and add resolve-by-location API
Replace routes with source-qualified URLs now
Only keep existing routes and skip resolve API in this slice

questions.prompt: What is the MVP behavior for Skill Trust in this refactor?
questions.description: ADR-0001 says bare locators resolve to current approved content. Current Skillpack-managed creation stores a latest version only.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Treat newly created Skillpack-managed versions as auto-approved for now, store or derive the current approved version separately from latest, and make bare skill://skillpack/{handle} resolve to current approved. Defer review workflows and policy configuration.

options.label: Auto-approve Skillpack-managed versions and expose current approved semantics
Add manual approval state and review endpoints now
Only document trust and skip code changes for approval semantics

questions.prompt: What should count as done for this goal?
questions.description: This should be concrete enough that another agent can implement and verify it.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Done means the codebase exposes north-star terminology in schemas/services/presenters, Skillpack-managed skills have stable skill:// locations, resolving a Skill Location returns a Resolved Skill with content and resource manifest, current approved semantics are represented for Skillpack-managed versions, existing UI/API flows still work, and checks pass.

options.label: Shared contracts and backend DTOs use north-star concepts clearly
Resolve API accepts skill://skillpack/{handle} and returns a Resolved Skill
Current approved semantics exist for Skillpack-managed skills
Existing catalog/detail/resource UI and API flows continue to work
pnpm check, typecheck, and build pass
